reason: The status board joins local WE backlog numbers and WE commit subjects to the WE lane plan; its PR links belong to that backlog.

Build/fix dispatch observers read WE PRs by WE backlog item key and WE lane head refs (`gh pr list/view` in the WE checkout); build dispatch is item-keyed and WE-only by construction, and a non-WE fix/ci-heal is refused upstream as `unsupported-repo` before reaching this file.
This is the ONE authoritative table where constellation owner-qualified repository slugs are defined for all consumers.
The systemd Documentation URL points to the daemon source hosted in WE; the scheduled target repository is separately supplied through cfg.repo.

The `pr-land` argv builders run gh with `cwd` bound to the checkout being landed from, so gh infers the repo from that checkout's git remote (any repo, not a hard-coded one); adding `--repo` would break the byte-identical argv `pr-land.mjs` executed before this port.

The flagged text sits inside a rubric criterion's own PROSE, naming `gh pr create`/`gh pr merge` as EXAMPLES of a raw command that duplicates a declared operation; nothing here executes gh, so there is no invocation to make repo-explicit.

A PR-keyed CI heal is WE-only by construction — `reconcile-fix-dispatch` refuses a foreign repo as `unsupported-repo` long before this wrapper runs, and the flagged token is this module's own required-flag list, not a gh invocation.

A PR-keyed repair is WE-only by construction — `reconcile-fix-dispatch` refuses a foreign repo as `unsupported-repo` long before this wrapper runs, and the flagged token is this module's own required-flag list, not a gh invocation.

The land-advance fallback scope reader deliberately pins the WE slug: the scope fence it builds fences a WE lane clone's own changed files, and every cross-repo reader beside it already takes its slug from the PR row (`pr.slug`).
